narrative_purpose: Shows Darwin's atoll succession: as a volcanic island subsides, the reef keeps building upward, outliving the rock it started on — the deep-time origin of a reef platform.
subject: A three-stage left-to-right sequence of the same volcanic island shown at three moments. Stage one (left): a tall conical volcanic island with a thin fringing reef hugging its shore. Stage two (middle): the island is lower and partly sunk, with a wider reef standing off from it enclosing a lagoon between reef and shore. Stage three (right): the island has vanished beneath the surface, leaving a ring-shaped reef enclosing a central lagoon of open water. A faint dashed outline of the sinking island connects the three stages beneath the waterline.
scene: Open tropical sea shown in side-on cross-section across three stages, waterline consistent across the frame, reef always reaching up to the light.
camera: Wide side-elevation triptych in one continuous seascape, three stages evenly spaced.
light: Cyan glow along each living reef crest at the waterline, warm-neutral on the volcanic rock, indigo in the deep water below.
palette: Ocean teal water, cyan reef crest, stone-grey volcanic rock fading as it sinks, void indigo depths.
style: Painterly naturalist geological cross-section plate, calm and diagrammatic but organic.
detail_level: Clear reef crest and island silhouette at each stage; simple graded water framed by deep negative space.
composition: Three evenly spaced stages left-to-right with open water band above for stage callouts (fringing, barrier, atoll).
consistency_notes: The reef crest stays at the waterline across all three stages while the island sinks — that persistence is the whole point. Keep the reef palette consistent with earlier figures.
